With `settings.PREPEND_WWW` true and a host not beginning with `"www."`, the layer redirects at once to the www. host, with any slash the path needs: /plain leaves, never reaching C, as one 301 to /plain/ on the www. host (`django/middleware/common.py:CommonMiddleware.process_request`, `django/http/request.py:HttpRequest.get_host`).

With `settings.APPEND_SLASH` true, the default, `CommonMiddleware.should_redirect_with_slash` asks whether a path without a final slash fails to resolve, resolves with one, and leads to a view without the `"should_append_slash"` mark of `no_append_slash` ([View decorators](../views/decorators.md#marks)); if so, the 404 becomes a redirect to the path with its slash (`django/middleware/common.py:CommonMiddleware.should_redirect_with_slash`).

On the way out only a request that has already ended in a 404 pays for it, and the way in makes it only when a redirect for `settings.PREPEND_WWW` is being sent anyway; made there always, it would resolve every path without a slash before the handler did (`django/middleware/common.py:CommonMiddleware.process_request`).

A leading `"//"` becomes `"/%2F"` through `escape_leading_slashes`, lest a browser take the `"Location"` for another host's (CVE-2018-14574, `docs/releases/1.11.15.txt`; `django/middleware/common.py:CommonMiddleware.get_full_path_with_slash`, `django/utils/http.py:escape_leading_slashes`).

Then a response that is not streaming and lacks a Content-Length is given its body's length; a stream gets none (`django/middleware/common.py:CommonMiddleware.process_response`).
`GZipMiddleware.process_response` compresses a response for a client that reads gzip (`django/middleware/gzip.py:GZipMiddleware.process_response`).

Only then does it add Accept-Encoding to `"Vary"`, before reading the client's Accept-Encoding, since from there what is sent depends on that header: 199 bytes leave with no `"Vary"` even for a client that sent gzip, and 400 bytes for a client that sent no Accept-Encoding leave uncompressed but varying on it (`django/utils/cache.py:patch_vary_headers`).

The compressed response keeps the uncompressed one's tag, and RFC 9110, section 8.8.1, which the code's comment cites, calls weak a validator sent alike for a representation with the gzip coding and for one without; the weak tag still matches an If-None-Match, which is compared weakly (`django/utils/cache.py:_if_none_match_passes`).

The compressors vary the length by up to `GZipMiddleware.max_random_bytes` bytes, against the BREACH attack ([Text helpers: `Truncator` and `django/utils/text.py`](../utils/text.md#compressing-a-response)).
`BrokenLinkEmailsMiddleware.process_response` tells the site's managers about a 404 while `settings.DEBUG` is false (`django/middleware/common.py:BrokenLinkEmailsMiddleware.process_response`).
`BrokenLinkEmailsMiddleware.is_ignorable_request` first lets the request go if (`django/middleware/common.py:BrokenLinkEmailsMiddleware.is_ignorable_request`):
the `"Referer"`'s path is the full path requested, and its host this one or no host at all, as some bots send to pass the first test (`docs/releases/1.9.txt`);

Otherwise `mail_managers` mails `settings.MANAGERS` through the default mailer unless, with `MAILERS` defined, `BrokenLinkEmailsMiddleware.using` names another ([Sending email: `mailers` and the email backends](../services/mailers.md)) (`django/middleware/common.py:BrokenLinkEmailsMiddleware.send_mail`).
The subject says "Broken INTERNAL link" when the `"Referer"` is on this host, a subdomain counting as another (`django/middleware/common.py:BrokenLinkEmailsMiddleware.is_internal_request`).

`BrokenLinkEmailsMiddleware` must stand outside every layer that turns a 404 into something else, a redirect from `LocaleMiddleware` or `CommonMiddleware`, a page from `FlatpageFallbackMiddleware` (`docs/howto/error-reporting.txt`).

The report was once `CommonMiddleware`'s; Django 1.6 moved it into `BrokenLinkEmailsMiddleware` for what its release notes call intractable ordering problems with `LocaleMiddleware` (`docs/releases/1.6.txt`).

With `MAILERS` defined, `BrokenLinkEmailsMiddleware.send_mail` drops `fail_silently=True` and passes over only `MailerDoesNotExist`: a failing mailer's error leaves `process_response`, and the wrapper makes the 404 a 500 (`docs/howto/mailers-migration.txt`).
